In any $2\times2\times2$ block, the eight cells realize each of the $2^3=8$ parity patterns exactly once. The condition "at least two coordinates even" selects exactly four of these eight patterns, so every $2\times2\times2$ block contains precisely $4$ black cubes.

Counting these cubes:
- all three coordinates even: $(N+1)^3$ choices,
- exactly two coordinates even: $3\cdot N(N+1)^2$ choices.

Hence the number of black cubes is
$$(N+1)^3+3N(N+1)^2=(N+1)^2(N+1+3N)=(N+1)^2(4N+1).$$

This equals $4N^3+9N^2+6N+1$ and is optimal.
